title: Four finite-level corners
statement:
Use the adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]: $A$ is Noetherian, $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$, $A/I$ is torsion, and $P_n=A/I^n$ is finite as a set and perfect over $A$ for every $n\geq1$. On a scheme $T$, the coefficient sheaves are $(P_n)_T$ and $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$, and $D(T_{\Proet},A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\Proet},A_T))$. All tensors with $P_n$ below mean derived extension of scalars along $A_T\to(P_n)_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], so their values are objects over $(P_n)_T$.

Let $\square$ be the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$
with $f$ proper. For every arrow $u:U\to V$ of the square, specialize [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] to the finite ring tower $Q_n=P_n=A/I^n$. This supplies specified ring isomorphisms
$$
 c_u:u^{-1}A_V\xrightarrow{\sim}A_U,\qquad
 c_{u,n}:u^{-1}(P_n)_V\xrightarrow{\sim}(P_n)_U,
$$
compatible with the projections $\pi_{T,n}:A_T\to(P_n)_T$, the quotient transitions, and composition of arrows. Explicitly $\pi_{U,n}c_u=c_{u,n}u^{-1}\pi_{V,n}$. These are the coefficient identifications used for the ordinary ringed-coefficient derived operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], at both integral and finite level. Let $K\in D(X_{\Proet},A)$ be derived $I$-complete [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. For $n\geq1$, a subscript $n$ on a pullback or direct image indicates coefficients $(P_n)_T$. Put
$$
 K_n=K\otimes_A^LP_n,\qquad E=L(g')^*K,
 \qquad E_n=L(g'_n)^*K_n.
$$
With these coefficient identifications, ordinary module pullback is exact [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and sends the coefficient module $(P_n)_X$ to $(P_n)_{X'}$, with its $A_{X'}$-action through $\pi_{X',n}$ by the displayed compatibility. Thus its derived pullback has the same identification, concentrated in degree zero. Apply the canonical ordinary pullback/tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $K$ and $(P_n)_X$. Together with the finite coefficient identification $c_{g',n}$ this identifies
$$
 E\otimes_A^LP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}E_n.
$$
The comparison is taken in $D(X'_{\Proet},P_n)$, retaining the quotient-coefficient action of derived extension of scalars: choose a K-flat representative $Q$ of $K$ with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Its pullback $(g')^*Q$ is K-flat with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and computes $E$ by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Both derived extensions of scalars are therefore computed by the displayed ordinary tensors [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. On these representatives the comparison is the natural tensor map
$$
 (g')^*Q\otimes_{A_{X'}}(P_n)_{X'}\ \cong\ (g'_n)^*(Q\otimes_{A_X}(P_n)_X),
$$
which is $(P_n)_{X'}$-linear because $c_{g'}$ and $c_{g',n}$ commute with the coefficient projections. For the quotient map $P_{n+1}\to P_n$, both composites with this tensor comparison send a local pure tensor $q\otimes p$ to the pullback of $q$ tensored with the quotient image of $p$. Equality on pure tensors gives equality of the sheaf maps, hence of the induced derived comparisons. Define four objects of $D(Y'_{\Proet},P_n)$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
 A_n&=Lg_n^*((Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP_n),&
 B_n&=Lg_n^*Rf_{*,n}K_n,\\
 C_n&=(Rf'_*E)\otimes_A^LP_n,&
 D_n&=Rf'_{*,n}E_n.
\end{aligned}
$$
Here $E$ is the ordinary pullback; no completed pullback is used in these four objects.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this four-corner datum: its
inputs are given separately by the completed pullback and its finite
reduction (Lemma 61.20.2, [Tag
099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N)), the proper base-change
isomorphism (Theorem 61.30.1, [Tag
09C9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9)) and the projection formula
that identifies $A_n$ with $B_n$ and $C_n$ with $D_n$ after tensoring with
the perfect coefficient $P_n$ (Equation 21.50.0.1, [Tag
0B56](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B56), with Lemma 21.50.1, [Tag
0944](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0944)), but no entry assembles
the four finite-level corners $A_n,B_n,C_n,D_n$ of one square; the blueprint
adds that assembly, at the finite coefficient rings $P_n=A/I^n$.

split_report.summary: Repaired C4/E1 by supplying compatible completed and finite coefficient inverse-image identifications through a general finite-ring-tower lemma. Explicitly specialized these to every square arrow, checked the coefficient-projection equation, and used exact identified-coefficient pullback to identify the derived pullback of P_n. The tensor comparison now retains its finite-ring action. Four objects and all hypotheses are preserved. Two new statement-only nodes; no definition proof steps.
split_report.blueprint: The displayed K_n, ordinary E, E_n and four formulas; the coefficient identifications needed by the ordinary operations and the canonical E reduction are explicit inputs, with their compatibility equations.
